**Aarhus Universitetshospital, Psykiatrien** is the overarching psychiatric center that houses [[bua|Børne- og Ungdomspsykiatrisk Afdeling (BUA)]] and employs both the chairman and co-chairman of the steering group, making it a key institutional environment for ADHD quality work in Denmark [^src1]. 

The organization's structure encompasses both child and youth psychiatric services as well as adult psychiatric services. Within the child and youth sector, BUA operates several specialized sub-clinics: the [[bua-psykiatrisk-klinik-for-skoleboern|BUA Psykiatrisk Klinik for Skolebørn]] [^src3], the [[bua-smaborn-klinik|BUA Psykiatrisk Klinik for Småbørn]] [^src3], the [[bua-psykiatrisk-klinik-for-unge|BUA Psykiatrisk Klinik for Unge]] [^src3], and the [[bua-psykiatrisk-klinik-for-udredning|BUA Psykiatrisk Klinik for Udredning]] [^src3]. On the adult side, the hospital operates a dedicated Team for ADHD within clinic 2 of the department for psychoses [^src2].

Several prominent figures in Danish ADHD treatment are employed by the hospital. These include [[shelagh-powell|Shelagh Powell]], a senior physician in Team 2 for school child psychiatry at BUA [^src1], and [[simon-hjerrild|Simon Hjerrild]], a senior physician, clinical lecturer, and PhD who works with the adult Team for ADHD and is affiliated with [[dps-midtjylland|DPS Midtjylland]] [^src1] [^src3]. 

Within the broader context of the national ADHD database annual reports, Aarhus Universitetshospital, Psykiatrien operates against a backdrop of systemic challenges in Danish psychiatry. These include increasing waiting times, low national target fulfillment, and significant regional disparities—most notably a severe decline in the number of treatment courses in Region Midtjylland, where the hospital is based.
